company_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, CET1 retention on risk-weighted-asset growth, AT1 and preference distributions charged in the flow

equity_bridge.item: Proceeds of the September 2026 A-share private placement (up to RMB100bn, MOF RMB70bn), priced at market
equity_bridge.note: Board-approved, pending EGM/NFRA/CSRC; the ~11,800m new shares are already in shares_outstanding. The cash raises CET1 by ~33bp and funds RWA growth that would otherwise be retained out of FY2027-28 earnings. Issued at ~0.76x H1 2026 BVPS, so BVPS-dilutive by ~0.8%; per-share FCFE value is roughly neutral.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: terminal nominal growth for the largest mature Chinese state bank (China nominal GDP ~4-5% less continued NIM drift and policy-priced lending), bracketed by revenue 5yr CAGR 0.0% and BVPS 5yr CAGR 7.7%; the DCF's base revenue path runs 4.0% -> 3.0%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Ordinary equity 3yr/5yr CAGR 7.1%/7.7% vs revenue -1.6%/0.0% and EPS 1.0%/3.1% (>30% apart). Equity growth is retained earnings on a flat share count (payout ~31%), not operating growth: revenue stalled because NIM fell from 2.11% (FY2021) to 1.28% (FY2025) while the balance sheet grew ~8-10%/yr. Equity CAGR is NOT used as the growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null: a bank's reported FCF (OCF - capex) is deposit-flow noise (415bn FY2021, 1,908bn FY2025). The relevant series is net profit attributable to ordinary shareholders: 350,900 (FY2024) -> 356,798 (FY2025), +1.7%, with H1 2026 +2.9%. Ordinary equity FY2020-FY2025 from the kpis table; BVPS 7.48 -> 10.83 RMB. Dividend payout 31.3% (2023), 31.3% (2024), 31.0% (2025) of ordinary profit.

scenario_narratives.base: NIM stabilises at ~1.28%, credit cost ~0.45%, operating income grows 3-4% and RWA growth slows from 7% to 3%. FCFE rises from ~RMB13bn (FY2026E, far below the RMB115bn dividend) to ~RMB85bn in FY2027 and ~RMB300bn by FY2036 as capital retention falls; terminal ROE ~7.6%, terminal P/B ~0.7x. CET1 held at 13.2% after the RMB100bn placement.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Chinese credit cycle turns: NIM recovers 5-10bp, credit cost falls to ~0.4%, cost-to-income ~28%, RWA growth 3.5-6.5%. FCFE ~RMB120bn in FY2027 rising to ~RMB400bn; terminal ROE ~8.8%; payout can rise above 30% without further state equity.
scenario_narratives.bear: Credit cost rises to ~0.7% on property/LGFV/retail losses while NIM compresses toward 1.1%; profit falls ~15%; RWA keeps growing on policy lending so FCFE is ~RMB35-45bn for two years, a third of the dividend. Either the dividend is cut, CET1 drifts toward the minimum, or a second discounted capital raise dilutes; terminal ROE ~5.9%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is worth the equity cash flow it can distribute after funding its own capital requirement, discounted at the cost of equity. For ICBC that flow is net profit to ordinary shareholders (after tax, NCI, preference dividends and perpetual-bond coupons) less the equity retained to hold CET1 at 13.2% on growing risk-weighted assets. Today that FCFE (~RMB13bn) is a small fraction of the ~RMB128bn the Bank pays out, so the headline 4.8% dividend yield is financed by capital-ratio drift and, from September 2026, by state equity issued at 0.76x book; the model credits only the FCFE and lets it rise as RWA growth decelerates. Net debt is zero by construction; deposits are operating funding. The H share trades at 0.58x book; the model's base terminal P/B is ~0.7x, consistent with a ~7.6% ROE at a 9.5% cost of equity.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: real-estate loan NPL 5.39% (FY2025) rising to ~6.27% (mid-2026), personal NPL 1.77% up from 1.63% in six months, H1 2026 impairment +22%; a credit cost of ~0.7% of loans takes the pre-tax margin to ~44% and FCFE to a third of the dividend (bear case).

Capital: CET1 13.21% at H1 2026, down 89bp in 18 months with the dividend far exceeding FCFE; the September 2026 placement is priced at ~0.76x book and a further round on the same terms is the dilution the flat post-placement share count does not model.

NIM: 2.11% (FY2021) to 1.28% (FY2025), 1.29% H1 2026; the FY2026 revenue jump is a one-time deposit-repricing benefit, and further LPR cuts without matching deposit repricing resume the compression (bear revenue path).

Policy-directed lending ('Five Priorities', LGFV resolution, property stabilisation) allocates RWA to state objectives rather than return; RWA grew 10% in FY2025 on ~8% loan growth and return on RWA has fallen from 1.68% to 1.37%.

Governance and currency: majority Huijin/MOF control, no buyback lever, payout set by policy (~30-31%); RMB flows against an HKD quote - a 10% RMB move is a 10% move in the HKD value; 10% H-share dividend withholding tax is not modelled.

The placement assumption (RMB100bn at CNY 8.48, ~11.8bn new shares, proceeds bridged) rests on external reporting in 1398.HK_Analysis.json, not on a filing; if only the MOF's RMB70bn is issued, or it is priced at a premium as in the 2025 round, the share count and bridge both shrink proportionally and the per-share value is roughly unchanged.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (1398.HK, HKD) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 5.78-7.77. FX CNYHKD=X, USDCNY=X, USDHKD=X and 601398.SS from the same API on the same date.
data_sources.financials: 1398.HK_Metrics.csv / metrics_normalized (FY2017-FY2025 annual, H1 2023-H1 2026 interim, Q1/Q3 2024-2026 quarterly, RMB millions) built from the HKEX annual, interim and quarterly reports in Extracted/; kpis table for ordinary shareholders' equity, BVPS, other equity instruments, dividends paid, credit impairment, NII, fee income, opex, cash taxes. FY2025 annual report: financial highlights (lines 544-597: RWA, ROE 9.45%, NIM 1.28%, cost-to-income 29.48%, coverage 213.60%), PBT 424,435 (line 508), EPS note (ordinary profit 356,798; preference dividends 4,997; perpetual coupons 6,767; lines 11839-11856), capital adequacy table (lines 5335-5342), dividend table (payout 31.0%, line ~8555), preference dividend table (line 6447). H1 2026 interim: income statement summary (lines 600-610: PBT 210,010, tax 33,535, NCI 2,793), NIM table (lines 615-660), capital table (lines 4116-4123: CET1 13.21%, RWA 29,832,780), ordinary profit 169,268 (line 6434), share capital 86,795m H + 269,612m A (lines 7948-7949), interim dividend RMB1.511/10 shares (line 206), outlook (line 4202).
data_sources.qualitative: 1398.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-17), read after the drivers were drafted and before the build; it supplied the September 2026 RMB300bn special-treasury-bond recapitalisation (ICBC placement up to RMB100bn, MOF RMB70bn, at market, 5-year lock-up), G-SIB bucket 3, real-estate NPL ~6.27% mid-2026, and confirmed NIM-stabilisation and ~30% payout guidance. Outlook and risk context also taken directly from the FY2025 annual report chairman/president statements (lines 764-875) and the H1 2026 interim outlook (line 4202).

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E operating income, RMB m: H1 2026 actual 446,163 (interim p.12-13, +9.1% YoY: NII +8.8% on deposit cost 1.45% -> 1.15%, non-interest income +9.9%) + H2 2026E ~409,000 (H2 2025 actual 392,313 x ~1.04; NIM 1.29% held, fee income seasonally lower in H2). FY2025 actual 801,395; FY2024 786,126. Revenue = net interest income + net fee and commission income + other non-interest income, the Bank's 'operating income' line.
inputs.share_count_basis: 356,406,257,089 A + H ordinary shares on the register at 30 June 2026 (269,612m A + 86,795m H, interim line 7948-7949; unchanged since 2017; basic = diluted EPS) PLUS ~11,800m new A shares for the September 2026 board-approved private placement of up to RMB100bn (MOF subscribing RMB70bn under the RMB300bn special-treasury-bond recapitalisation; priced 'at market value', modelled at the 601398.SS close of CNY 8.48, 5-year lock-up; see 1398.HK_Analysis.json recent_developments). The placement is post-balance-sheet and subject to EGM/NFRA/CSRC approval; the 2025 round for BOC/CCB/BOCOM/PSBC completed within ~3 months, so it is treated as done and the RMB100bn proceeds are added in equity_bridge. One class, same economic rights, so the per-share value applies to the H share. Otherwise FLAT: preference shares convert only on a CET1 trigger (5.125%), SBC-zero, no buybacks.
inputs.debt_cash_note: Bank: customer deposits (RMB37.3tn), interbank funding, central-bank borrowings and debt securities issued (~RMB2.6tn average H1 2026) are operating funding, and cash/central-bank balances are liquidity, not surplus. Net debt is zero by construction on the FCFE route; nothing is bridged after the flows except the new-share proceeds.
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is FY2026E FCFE = net profit attributable to ORDINARY shareholders ~RMB360bn (PBT ~436bn at a 51.0% pre-tax margin, less income tax, NCI and other-equity-instrument distributions at 17.5%) LESS capital retained to hold CET1 at 13.2% on ~9.3% RWA growth (0.093 x 0.132 x 28,269,948 = ~347bn). That is ~RMB13bn against ~RMB115bn of ordinary dividends plus ~RMB13bn of AT1/preference coupons: the gap is why CET1 fell from 14.10% (FY2024) to 13.57% (FY2025) to 13.21% (H1 2026) and why the state is injecting RMB70-100bn. Reported OCF - capex (FY2025: 1,956,738 - 48,979) is deposit and interbank flow noise and is not used.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero: state-owned bank, no share-based payment scheme disclosed in the FY2018-FY2025 annual reports (ShareRepurchases 0 every period, StockBasedComp 0 in the CSV); basic = diluted EPS (RMB1.00 FY2025). House and street bases coincide; band_position is degenerate.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts CNY (model; the Bank reports in RMB) to HKD (H-share quote): CNYHKD=X 1.1727 at 2026-10-16T11:34Z, Yahoo Finance. Triangulated against USDCNY=X 6.6755 / USDHKD=X 7.8482 = 1.1757 (same source, same date; 0.3% apart). The Shanghai A share (601398.SS) closed at CNY 8.48 = HKD 9.94 on 2026-10-16, a ~31% A/H premium that is normal for Chinese state banks, so the dual listing is not a parity check. Per-share values are per ordinary share and apply equally to A and H shares.
inputs.fy0: FY2026E (year ending 2026-12-31, unreported: H1 2026 actual + H2 estimate)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z HKEX regular close (Friday); valuation dated the following Saturday
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-06-30 (register) plus the September 2026 placement, see share_count_basis
inputs.cet1_anchor: CET1 ratio 13.21% on RWA RMB29,832,780m at 30 Jun 2026 (interim lines 4116-4121); 13.57% on 28,269,948m at FY2025 (AR lines 5335-5340); 14.10% on 25,710,855m at FY2024. RWA grew 4.3% FY2024, 10.0% FY2025, 5.5% in H1 2026 alone. G-SIB bucket 3 from 2026 (2.0% surcharge): CET1 minimum 5.0% + 2.5% conservation + 2.0% = 9.5%, so the Bank carries a ~3.7pt buffer. Tier 1 14.43%, total CAR 18.57%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single CNY cost of equity 9.5% in every scenario (risk is charged once, through the scenario weights, not by moving the discount rate), the same rate used for the sibling Big Four bank 0939.HK (CCB); 0998.HK (CITIC, a joint-stock bank with a 9.4% CET1) carries 10.5%. Built in the flows' own currency: 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8% (ASSUMPTION: not fetched; the PBOC easing cycle has had the 10Y CGB in the 1.6-2.0% range since 2025) + beta ~1.05 x China ERP ~6.5% = ~8.6%, plus ~0.9pt for the risks a CSI-300 ERP does not price for an H-share holder: state-directed lending ('Five Priorities', LGFV and property-stabilisation mandates), majority Huijin/MOF control with the payout set by policy and no buyback lever, a state recapitalisation at 0.76x book, and capital-account/RMB convertibility risk. Not higher than CCB: ICBC is the largest G-SIB, CET1 13.2% with a 3.7pt buffer, NPL 1.29%, coverage 218%. Hurdle for entry price is the house 15%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Bank: IFRS 16 right-of-use depreciation and lease-liability interest (RMB19,551m lease liabilities at FY2025, AR line 13329) sit inside operating expenses, i.e. inside the pre-tax margin. lease_cost_pct_path is zero so the charge is not taken twice; nothing is deducted as debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, inside the 'cash_tax_rate' deduction: the margin is calibrated to PROFIT BEFORE TAX (424,435 FY2025, after credit impairment 132,973) and the deduction rate covers income tax (53,669; 12.6%), profit attributable to non-controlling interests (2,204; 0.5%) and distributions on other equity instruments (11,764; 2.8% - preference dividends 4,997 + perpetual-bond coupons 6,767, AR lines 11839-11840). FY2025 total 15.9% = (424,435 - 356,798) / 424,435, where 356,798 is net profit attributable to ordinary shareholders (AR line 11856). H1 2026 ran at 16.0% tax + 1.3% NCI + 2.1% perpetual coupons (prefs are paid in H2), so FY2026E is set at 17.5%. Other equity instruments (RMB364,666m at H1 2026) and NCI (20,978m) are therefore NOT deducted again in a bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> dcf-methods routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift'. Run as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the house precedent for banks (0939.HK CCB and 0998.HK CITIC this month; HSBC, LYG, WF, MFG, HDB, IBN, BMO, USB, WFC, NAB.AX). First valuation of this ticker, no MEMORY.md entry. Not an owner-FCF DCF: deposits are operating funding, OCF is meaningless (443bn FY2021, 1,957bn FY2025), net debt is zero by construction and no debt or cash is bridged. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = operating income; ebitda_margin = pre-tax profit margin (after credit impairment, which is the real cost of a bank); sbc, D&A, leases and working capital all zero; cash_tax_rate = income tax + NCI + AT1/preference distributions, so EBIT x (1 - rate) = net profit to ORDINARY shareholders; capex = equity retained to hold CET1 at 13.2% on RWA growth (g_RWA x 13.2% x prior-year RWA, as % of revenue), so FCF = FCFE = distributable earnings. Terminal growth applies to FCFE at the cost of equity; terminal_cap_multiple 18x FCFE is above the Gordon multiple in every scenario (15.4x base, 17.3x bull, 14.6x bear) and does not bind. KEY FINDING: FY2026E FCFE ~RMB13bn is far BELOW the ~RMB128bn of ordinary dividends plus AT1/preference coupons the Bank pays; CET1 fell 89bp in 18 months and the state is now recapitalising (RMB70bn MOF, up to RMB100bn total, Sept 2026). The dividend is being funded by capital-ratio drift and new equity, and the valuation credits only the FCFE, which ramps from ~RMB85bn (FY2027) to ~RMB300bn (FY2036) as RWA growth slows from ~9% to 3%. QUALITATIVE CONTEXT: 1398.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-17) landed while the drivers were being set and was read before the build; it supplied the September 2026 placement (modelled in the share count and equity_bridge) and confirms the driver paths (NIM stabilising ~1.28-1.29% with no numeric target; payout ~30%; Five Priorities lending growing faster than the book; real-estate NPL 5.39% rising to ~6.27%; personal NPL 1.77% at H1 2026 up from 1.63%). Drivers rest on the FY2025 annual report (operating income 801,395, PBT 424,435, NIM 1.28%, NPL 1.31%, coverage 213.6%, cost-to-income 29.48%, ROE 9.45%, dividend RMB3.103/10 shares = 31.0% of ordinary profit) and the H1 2026 interim (operating income +9.1%, impairment +22.2% to 127,756, PBT +5.5%, ordinary profit 169,268 +2.9%, NIM 1.29% -1bp YoY, NPL 1.29%, coverage 217.6%, cost-to-income 23.70%, ROE 8.63% annualised, interim dividend RMB1.511/10 shares). Revenue was flat FY2020-FY2025 (800,075 -> 801,395, 0.0% CAGR) while RWA grew ~6-7%/yr, so return on RWA fell from 1.68% to 1.37%. The H share trades at 0.58x H1 2026 BVPS (RMB11.12) and a 4.8% pre-withholding FY2025 dividend yield. Valuation date is 9.5 months into FY2026, so FY2026E is fy0 (not discounted) and the first discounted flow is FY2027; the FY2025 final dividend (60.2bn, July 2026) and FY2026 interim (~53.9bn, Jan 2027) are paid out of fy0 and are not double-counted.

bear.growth_rationale: NIM resumes compressing toward 1.10% (further LPR cuts, deposit costs sticky after the repricing windfall), fee income flat; revenue repeats the FY2021-25 stall.
bear.margin_rationale: Credit cost rises to ~0.7% of loans in FY2027-28 (real-estate NPL already 6.3%, LGFV restructuring, personal NPL 1.77% and rising) - the FY2020 margin was 50.1% at credit cost 0.9% but on a 2.1% NIM; at a 1.2% NIM the same credit cost takes the margin to ~44% - then partly recovers to 47%.
bear.capex_rationale: Policy-directed lending keeps RWA growing 7.0, 6.0, 5.0, 5.0, 4.5, 4.0, 3.5, 3.0, 2.5, 2.5% while earnings fall; CET1 held at 13.2% consumes ~90% of ordinary profit in FY2027-28 (FCFE ~RMB35-45bn against a ~RMB110bn dividend). In practice this is the scenario where the dividend is cut, CET1 is allowed to drift toward the 9.5% minimum, or a second discounted state recapitalisation dilutes the H share; the flat post-placement share count understates the damage. Terminal ROE ~5.9%.
bear.tax_rationale: Fixed AT1/preference coupons against a smaller PBT.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon 1.025/0.07 = 14.6x FCFE; cap does not bind.
bear.narrative: A credit-cost cycle plus renewed NIM compression. Earnings fall ~15%, the capital ratio cannot support both policy-pace growth and the dividend, and value accrues to the state's lending priorities rather than minority H-share holders.

base.growth_rationale: Operating income +4% for two years then 3.5% and 3%: the FY2026 jump (+6-7%) is a deposit-repricing windfall (deposit cost 1.45% -> 1.15%) that fades as the asset side keeps repricing down to the LPR; NIM holds ~1.25-1.30%, balance sheet grows ~7% slowing to ~4%, fee income flat-to-up (H1 2026 +3.3%). Below RWA growth, so return on RWA keeps drifting down.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax margin after credit impairment. FY2023 52.3%, FY2024 53.7%, FY2025 53.0%, FY2026E ~51.0% (H1 47.1% vs 48.6% a year earlier as impairment rose 22%; H2 is seasonally ~8-9pt higher because ICBC front-loads provisions). Base holds 50.5%: credit cost ~0.45% of loans, cost-to-income ~29-30%, real-estate (NPL 5.4-6.3%) and personal (NPL 1.77%) books absorbing a bit more provisioning each year, no NIM recovery.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retained to hold CET1 at 13.2% on RWA growth of 7.0, 6.5, 6.0, 5.5, 5.0, 4.5, 4.0, 3.5, 3.0, 3.0% from FY2026E RWA RMB30,900bn (FY2025 28,270bn, H1 2026 29,833bn). RWA grew 4.3% FY2024, 10.0% FY2025, 5.5% in H1 2026; the Five Priorities mandate keeps the book growing faster than nominal GDP for several more years. Retention / revenue: 0.07 x 0.132 x 30,900,000 / 889,200 = 32.1% in FY2027, falling to 16.0% as RWA growth converges on terminal growth. Terminal-year (FY2036) RWA ~RMB49.3tn, CET1 capital ~6.5tn; terminal ROE ~7.6%.
base.tax_rationale: Income tax ~13.5% (FY2025 12.6%, H1 2026 16.0%; low because of tax-exempt government-bond interest, which is a shrinking share as the investment book shifts) + NCI ~1.0% + other-equity-instrument distributions ~3.0% (perpetual coupons ~9bn on RMB250-270bn of perps plus RMB4.2bn of domestic preference dividends) = 17.5% of PBT, held flat. Coupons are fixed in RMB, so the percentage falls slightly as PBT grows; ignored (conservative).
base.terminal_note: Gordon on FY2036 FCFE at 9.5% - 3.0% = 15.4x; the 18x cap does not bind in any scenario. It binds only in the sensitivity grid's low cost-of-equity rows, which is the cap doing its job: a bank earning ~7.6% on equity is not worth 20x its distributable earnings. Implied terminal P/B ~0.7x on terminal ROE ~7.6%, consistent with (ROE - g)/(CoE - g).
base.narrative: Steady-state state bank: NIM holds ~1.28%, credit cost ~0.45%, RWA growth decelerates from 7% to 3% and the dividend becomes fully covered by FCFE around FY2029-30. CET1 held at 13.2% after the RMB100bn placement.

bull.growth_rationale: NIM recovers 5-10bp as deposit repricing completes and the PBOC easing cycle ends; fee income grows mid-single digits (wealth management AUM RMB25tn, custody, investment banking); overseas/subsidiary income (10.1% of the total) grows faster; balance sheet grows ~6%.
bull.margin_rationale: Credit cost back to ~0.40%, cost-to-income ~28% on AI-driven efficiency, property book stabilises; 53.5% is the FY2024-25 margin.
bull.capex_rationale: CET1 held at 13.2% on RWA growth of 6.5, 6.0, 5.5, 5.0, 4.5, 4.0 then 3.5% (advanced-approach RWA savings, slower policy lending). Terminal ROE ~8.8%.
bull.tax_rationale: Fixed AT1/preference coupons fall to ~2.5% of a larger PBT.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon 1.035/0.06 = 17.3x FCFE; cap 18x does not bind.
bull.narrative: China's credit cycle turns, NIM and credit cost both improve, RWA growth slows to 3.5% and the payout ratio can rise above 30% without eroding CET1 or needing further state equity.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30%, the same as the sibling 0939.HK (CCB) and below the 35% used for the joint-stock 0998.HK: ICBC has the thickest CET1 buffer of the three (13.2%, ~3.7pt above its G-SIB-bucket-3 minimum) and the state has just shown it will recapitalise, but the dividend already exceeds FCFE by ~RMB100bn a year, RWA grew 10% in FY2025 and 5.5% in H1 2026 on policy lending, real-estate NPL is 6.3% and rising, personal NPL is up 14bp in six months and H1 impairment rose 22%. Bull 20%: NIM has only just stopped falling and the Five Priorities mandate caps upside. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
